chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Police harassment and the Baltimore jail in 1941
summary: Police harassed musicians; in 1941 Smith and Eddie Durham's band was jailed overnight in Baltimore after a mixed-audience raid.

bands.name: Eddie Durham and Buster Smith's band

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: It was really that bad.
Yeah. Yeah, they sure did. And the police used to be awful bad on musicians back in them 20's and 30's.
In what sort of way?

They really got on you. You couldn't bat your eyes. They'd put you in jail. In these little towns, down in these Southern towns, many of them down the highway. You could be in the (?) state somewhere and be tryin' to make it to a dancehall and you're a little late; they'll stop you and give you a speeding ticket. And they don't care what time you got to be there. It don't make no difference to them anyway. They'll mess with you, they'll put you in jail.
Did they ever put you in jail?
Yeah, yeah, they put you in jail.
When were you in jail?
Buster Smith - 150
Oh, sure. They put Eddie Durham almost in jail in Baltimore.
Was this with the Blue Devils?
No. Eddie Durham and I, we had a band. Went down through and played a theatre there...
When was this?
It was in '41, I believe it was.
That was the band that made those records.

Mmm-hmm. Yeah, we went down there. We got through playing that night at the theatre, and they invited us down... The hotel had a big nightclub down in the basement. And these... It wasn't the Ink Spots. Some more boys... They was a singing group who was famous, and they was down there that night, working down there. And everybody went down there at the end. The house was just packed. So everybody wanted to come down there to hear these boys sing. So White people and Colored and all were down there together, and the law come in there and raid the place because Coloreds and Whites was in there together. The Whites were sitting one side of the house and then the Coloreds was on the other side, but they raided it anyhow. Then they killed the band and put the band in jail!
You were in the band?
Yeah, because we was down there! And of course, we had to stay in there all night. Then the boy with the big
Buster Smith - 151
upright bass, he was in jail with his bass in there, and then so many men in there, they couldn't turn around. He had to stand up and hold that bass...
All night.
Yeah, all night. Hold it up against the wall. Then the next morning, the judge come down, and Eddie came down and told the judge what happened, and that judge made them turn us loose.
Without charges or anything.
Yeah, no charges.
Crazy.
Yeah, you'd run into all that kind of stuff.
